[asking for a friend  ]
Thanks in advance

She can play Piper, but not in order to recruit a Nephandus since she doesn't play (=from your hand) the Nephandus in that case. Mata Hari only mimicks the clan when "playing" cards.

Messages.Body:
So the card (eg Nephandus) is not played but also not put into play.
How does it get onto the table? It states it gets recruited ...
Also: VTES One has a FAQ stating otherwise and isn‘t contradicted so far.
vtesone.wordpress.com/2008/09/07/vtes-rules-piper-qa/

Q: If “Mata Hari” is an Anarch, can I use to “Piper” to tap her and recruit an ally requiring a clan, e.g. a “War Ghoul” or “Renegade Garou“?
A: “Piper” requires that the Anarch tapped for the “Piper” fulfill the requirements for recruiting the ally, and “Mata Hari clearly can recruit all those allies requiring a clan.

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
> alf wrote:
> So the card (eg Nephandus) is not played but also not put into play.
> How does it get onto the table? It states it gets recruited ...
>
Exactly, that's why it ends up in play.

Recruiting an ally puts it in play.
Putting an ally in play puts it is play (but the ally is not recruited, so it can act the same turn for instance).
If you play an ally card to recruit that ally, then the ally is recruited and put in play. But there are other ways to recruit allies, such as Piper.

Messages.Author: Bloodartist
Messages.Body:
Vampire who plays piper, recruits the ally in question.

In order to recruit a nephandus, the vampire needs to be anti-tremere.

If Mata Hari would recruit a nephandus via piper, she doesn't count as anti-tremere for nephandus since Mata Hari is not playing the nephandus from your hand. Therefore it doesn't work.

This is decently straightforward imo..
